title: Problem Overview
content: Erdős Problem #105 asks whether $n - 3$ obstacle points can block all 'rich' lines through $n$ non-collinear points. A rich line contains $\geq 2$ points from the main set $A$. The conjecture was DISPROVED by Xichuan (2024) with three explicit counterexamples. The \$50 prize (offered by Erdős and Purdy) was awarded for the disproof.
mathContext: Given $|A| = n$ non-collinear, $|B| = n-3$: must $\exists$ line $\ell$ with $|\ell \cap A| \geq 2$ and $\ell \cap B = \emptyset$?

title: Points in the Plane
content: Points are elements of `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)`, the standard Mathlib representation of $\mathbb{R}^2$. This provides the full inner product space structure needed for affine geometry — distances, angles, and line parameterizations.

title: Line Representation
content: A line is represented parametrically: $\ell = \{p_0 + t \cdot d : t \in \mathbb{R}\}$ where $p_0$ is a base point and $d \neq 0$ is a direction vector. A point $p$ lies on $\ell$ iff $p = p_0 + t \cdot d$ for some $t \in \mathbb{R}$. This parametric form is natural for Lean formalization and avoids the complications of implicit line equations.
mathContext: $\ell = \{p_0 + td : t \in \mathbb{R}\}$ with $d \neq 0$; $p \in \ell \iff \exists t,\, p = p_0 + td$

title: Rich Lines
content: A line $\ell$ is *rich* for a set $A$ if $|\ell \cap A| \geq 2$, i.e., it passes through at least two points of $A$. Rich lines are the objects of interest: by the Szemerédi-Trotter theorem, $n$ non-collinear points determine $\Theta(n^2)$ rich lines, but most pass through exactly 2 points. The question is whether $n - 3$ obstacles can block all of them.
mathContext: $\ell \text{ is rich for } A \iff |\{a \in A : a \in \ell\}| \geq 2$

title: Unblocked Lines
content: A line is *unblocked* by $B$ if $\ell \cap B = \emptyset$ — no obstacle point lies on it. The central question is whether there always exists a line that is simultaneously rich (for $A$) and unblocked (by $B$). Each obstacle point can block at most the lines passing through it.
mathContext: $\ell \text{ unblocked by } B \iff \forall b \in B,\, b \notin \ell$

title: Non-Collinearity
content: A set $A$ is non-collinear if no single line contains all points of $A$, i.e., $\nexists \ell : A \subseteq \ell$. This is a crucial hypothesis: if $A$ were collinear, there would be exactly one rich line, and a single obstacle could block it. Non-collinearity ensures a rich structure of lines determined by $A$.

title: The Erdős-Purdy Conjecture
content: The conjecture (Erdős-Purdy, 1995): for disjoint $A, B \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ with $|A| = n$ (non-collinear) and $|B| = n - 3$, there must exist a rich line of $A$ that avoids $B$. The number $n - 3$ was chosen because Hickerson showed $n - 2$ obstacles can block all rich lines, so $n - 3$ was the natural 'boundary' case. Xichuan's disproof shows this boundary is also on the blocking side.
mathContext: $\forall A, B \subset \mathbb{R}^2,\, |A| = n,\, |B| = n-3,\, A \cap B = \emptyset,\, \text{NonCollinear}(A) \implies \exists \ell : |\ell \cap A| \geq 2 \land \ell \cap B = \emptyset$

title: Xichuan's Counterexample
content: Xichuan (2024) found three explicit counterexamples: point configurations where $A$ has $n$ non-collinear points, $B$ has $n - 3$ points, yet every rich line of $A$ passes through some point of $B$. The constructions exploit configurations where $A$ has few rich lines relative to its size, so $n - 3$ obstacles suffice to block all of them. This disproved the Erdős-Purdy conjecture and earned the \$50 prize.
mathContext: $\exists A, B : |A| = n \land |B| = n-3 \land \text{NonCollinear}(A) \land \forall \ell,\, |\ell \cap A| \geq 2 \implies \ell \cap B \neq \emptyset$

title: The Formal Disproof
content: Proves $\neg\text{ErdosPurdyConjecture}$ by contradiction: the conjecture would guarantee a rich unblocked line for Xichuan's counterexample, but that example was constructed so no such line exists. The proof destructures the counterexample axiom and derives the contradiction cleanly.

title: Hickerson's $n-2$ Construction
content: Before Xichuan, Hickerson showed that $n - 2$ obstacle points CAN block all rich lines of $n$ non-collinear points. This established that the 'critical case' was $n - 3$: either the boundary between blockable and non-blockable, or also blockable. Xichuan proved the latter, showing the transition happens at some lower threshold.

title: Beck-Szemerédi-Trotter Positive Result
content: With only $cn$ obstacle points (for some small constant $c > 0$), at least one rich line must be unblocked. This follows from the Szemerédi-Trotter incidence bound: $n$ non-collinear points determine $\Omega(n^2)$ rich lines, and $cn$ obstacles can block at most $O(cn \cdot n) = O(cn^2)$ lines (each obstacle lies on $O(n)$ lines). For $c$ small enough, some rich line survives.

title: Szemerédi-Trotter Theorem
content: The Szemerédi-Trotter theorem (1983): the number of incidences between $m$ points and $n$ lines in $\mathbb{R}^2$ is $O(m^{2/3}n^{2/3} + m + n)$. This is tight — matching constructions exist. The theorem is fundamental to discrete geometry and implies that $n$ points determine $\Omega(n)$ rich lines (with $\geq 2$ points each). The exponent $2/3$ is optimal by the Elekes-Rónyai construction.

title: The Threshold Function
content: The threshold function $f(n)$ is axiomatized as the largest number of obstacles that cannot block all rich lines of $n$ non-collinear points. Known bounds: $f(n) \geq cn$ for some $c > 0$ (Beck/Szemerédi-Trotter) and $f(n) \leq n - 4$ (from Xichuan's counterexample at $n - 3$). The gap between linear and $n - O(1)$ is the main remaining open question.
mathContext: $f(n) = \max\{k : \forall A, B,\, |A| = n \land |B| = k \implies \exists \text{ rich unblocked } \ell\}$, with $cn \leq f(n) \leq n - 4$

title: Open Problems
content: Two open problems are formalized: (1) `openProblem_n_minus_4`: does the conjecture hold with $n - 4$ obstacles? Xichuan disproved $n - 3$, Hickerson disproved $n - 2$, so $n - 4$ is the natural next case. (2) `openProblem_exact_threshold`: is $f(n) = \Theta(n)$? This asks whether there exist $c_1, c_2 > 0$ with $c_1 n \leq f(n) \leq c_2 n$ for all $n$.
mathContext: Open: $f(n) \stackrel{?}{\geq} n - 4$; $\exists c_1, c_2 > 0 : c_1 n \leq f(n) \leq c_2 n$?

title: Summary Theorem
content: `erdos_105_summary` is a proved theorem combining two results: (1) $\neg\text{ErdosPurdyConjecture}$ (the disproof via Xichuan) and (2) `beck_szemeredi_trotter_positive` ($cn$ obstacles cannot block all rich lines). The proof is `⟨erdos_105_disproved, beck_szemeredi_trotter_positive⟩`. Together, these establish that the transition from 'cannot block' to 'can block' lies strictly between $cn$ and $n - 3$.

title: Historical Timeline
content: 1983: Beck and Szemerédi-Trotter prove the incidence bound $I(P,L) = O(|P|^{2/3}|L|^{2/3} + |P| + |L|)$, implying the positive result with $cn$ obstacles. 1995: Erdős and Purdy conjecture the $n - 3$ version and offer a \$50 prize. Later: Hickerson shows $n - 2$ obstacles can block all rich lines. 2024: Xichuan disproves the $n - 3$ version with three explicit counterexamples, claiming the prize.
